article_title: Abnormal brain activation during speech perception and production in children and adults with reading difficulty
citation: Yang Fu, Xiaohui Yan, Jiaqi Mao, Haibin Su & Fan Cao. (2024). Abnormal brain activation during speech perception and production in children and adults with reading difficulty. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-024-00266-2
title: fNIRS foreign speech perception and production paradigm for detecting RD
description: A paired-task neuroimaging protocol combining a passive rapid event-related Spanish CV-syllable perception task (120 pairs varying in syllable consistency and similarity to Chinese, four runs of around 4 min) with a speech production imitation task (26 multi-syllabic Chinese pseudowords and 26 Spanish words, 156 trials), recorded with a 48-channel continuous-wave fNIRS system. The article uses it because "fNIRS is especially suitable for studying speech production, because of its relative tolerance with motion artifacts." Activation patterns from these tasks feed an SVM classifier that distinguishes RD from controls.
requirements: Participants must be native Chinese speakers who have not learned Spanish, so foreign-speech similarity to the native language can be controlled
constraints: The article notes the relatively small sample size and cross-sectional design might have limited the capability of revealing developmental changes
target_learners: Chinese children (fifth grade) and young adults with and without reading difficulty
target_learning_goals: Foreign (Spanish) speech perception and production as behavioral and neural indices of phonological processing in reading difficulty
examples: Participants listened to 120 pairs of Spanish consonant-vowel syllables and imitated 26 Chinese pseudowords and 26 Spanish words while HbO responses were recorded with a NIRSport2 system at 4.4 Hz
key_sources: Yang Fu, Xiaohui Yan, Jiaqi Mao, Haibin Su & Fan Cao. (2024). Abnormal brain activation during speech perception and production in children and adults with reading difficulty. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-024-00266-2

article_title: Development of Knowledge, Awareness, Global Warming Decreasing Behavior and Critical Thinking of Grade 11 Students Using the Four Noble Truths Method with Meta-Cognitive Techniques
citation: Sakkarin Chattuchai, Adisak Singseewo and Paitool Suksringarm. (2015). Development of knowledge, awareness, global warming decreasing behavior and critical thinking of grade 11 students using the Four Noble Truths method with meta-cognitive techniques. Educational Research and Reviews. https://doi.org/10.5897/ERR2015.2360
title: Five lesson plans on global warming using the FNT method with three metacognitive techniques
description: The study's instructional element is a set of five lesson plans on global warming, each consisting of three hours of learning per week, used over three weeks. The experimental plans use the FNT method with the three metacognitive techniques (intelligibility, plausibility, wide-applicability), while control plans use the traditional teaching method. Metacognitive questions were added to each stage of the FNT method in developing the plans.
requirements: Taught by the researcher over three weeks, three hours each, with instruments administered as pretest, immediate posttest and a four-week delayed posttest for behavior
examples: The two groups were taught by the researcher who used the 5 assigned lesson plans for three weeks, 3 h each
